I will not start from empty. I will do almost what I did last year, then adjust a little by price and how the weather has been. My land is 12 mu, and for my house with 2 people, I will keep the main part in wheat-maize because that is the steady way here, and I will leave a smaller part for cotton. Around me, if wheat and maize are managed too lightly, yield drops fast, and once yield is lost I cannot get it back. Fertilizer costs money, but losing harvest costs more, so I will not cut too hard. With well water in hand, I will make sure wheat gets the key irrigations, and maize gets water at the important growth stage. For wheat, I will keep 8 mu, use improved seed, put a solid base fertilizer and then topdress nitrogen when it needs strength. For maize after wheat, I will sow quickly on the same 8 mu, mostly keep no-tillage or very light tillage to save labor, and I will feed it enough nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer. Cotton gives cash, but it needs more watching, more pesticide, and more labor, so at my age I will not plant too much. I will keep it to 4 mu, use improved seed, fertilize it more evenly, and spray more times because insects on cotton are never light if I ignore them.
